subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in user-output file permission policy, and if so should it be expressed as process umask, explicit file/dir modes, or a narrower per-tool/shared-workspace mode policy?
rationale: The request is useful and vision-aligned, but it adds config surface and intentionally widens filesystem access for some outputs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Add an opt-in user-output policy
options.body: Define a narrow policy for user-created workspace/output artifacts, keep private state out of scope, and require schema, docs, and cross-path tests before implementation.

options.title: Document external host policy only
options.body: Close as not planned and point Docker/NAS operators to host ACL, bind-mount ownership, or post-processing tools instead of adding OpenClaw config surface.

options.title: Fix only one write surface
options.body: Narrow the work to Write/Edit or sandbox/media output and leave exec-created files to host process policy, accepting divergent behavior across tools.

recommendation.title: Add an opt-in user-output policy
recommendation.body: Define a narrow policy for user-created workspace/output artifacts, keep private state out of scope, and require schema, docs, and cross-path tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-confidence recent history is on sandbox filesystem-mode hardening, which is the most security-sensitive part of the requested boundary.
